key_insight: Agreement in annual capacity factor can mask substantial differences in predicted offshore wind wakes across distance, season, and atmospheric conditions.
engineering_relevance: Regional offshore wind energy assessments should account for wake-model formulation uncertainty when estimating output from densely developed wind farm clusters.
method: Evaluate a 100.7 GW North Sea offshore wind scenario for 2050 under year-round weather conditions.
Compare HARMONIE-AROME mesoscale simulations, ASPIRE large-eddy simulations, and three engineering wake models.
Assess Jensen, Bastankhah Gaussian, and TurbOPark predictions across downstream distances and atmospheric regimes.
evidence_signal: LES and mesoscale simulations reproduce observed local free-stream winds, while all three engineering models predict higher monthly mean wind speeds than LES, with biases reaching 0.60–0.70 m/s at 10–40 km downstream.
watch_item: Validation of local free-stream winds does not establish accuracy for regional wakes; model biases also depend on wind speed and atmospheric stability.
paper_title: Wake effects in a 100 GW North Sea offshore wind scenario: a model intercomparison under year-round weather conditions
